strings.name: Alan Jope
strings.role: Former Unilever CEO and chair of the Leverhulme Trust
strings.summary: Jope joined Unilever as a marketing trainee, led North Asia and Beauty & Personal Care, and served as group CEO from 2019 to 2023. His tenure included portfolio changes and the setback of a rejected bid for GSK's consumer healthcare business. After leaving, he moved into board service and academic research funding.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Led Unilever and contributed to global consumer brands and corporate sustainability practices.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Bachelor of Commerce with Honours, University of Edinburgh; Harvard Business School's General Management Program, which is not an MBA degree.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Consumer goods management across regions
strings.highlights.h1.text: Built marketing and operating experience in the UK, North America and Asia, progressing from China and North Asia leadership to Beauty & Personal Care president and then Unilever CEO.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Board service and research funding
strings.highlights.h2.text: Joined Accenture's board in 2023 and became chair of the Leverhulme Trust in 2024, taking leadership roles in corporate governance and academic research funding.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Visited Oxford as trust chair
strings.timeline.t1.text: Joined the Leverhulme Trust team at Oxford's demographic science centre to discuss research priorities and plans for the centre's sustainability beyond 2029.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Became chair of the Leverhulme Trust
strings.timeline.t2.text: After joining as a trustee in 2021, took over as chair in August 2024, contributing to the governance of the UK academic research funder.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Ended his Unilever tenure and joined a new board
strings.timeline.t3.text: Stepped down as Unilever CEO at the end of June. He had joined Accenture's board in April, beginning a shift toward non-executive and public affairs roles.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Consumer healthcare bid rejected
strings.timeline.t4.text: Unilever's roughly £50 billion proposal for GSK's consumer healthcare business was rejected, prompting investor questions about valuation, debt and group strategy.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Took over as Unilever CEO
strings.timeline.t5.text: Succeeded Paul Polman as leader of the multinational consumer goods company, a position he held until June 2023.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Led the personal care business
strings.timeline.t6.text: Began leading the business later known as Beauty & Personal Care, overseeing a major Unilever brand portfolio before becoming group CEO.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Took charge of China and North Asia
strings.timeline.t7.text: Started leading Unilever's China and North Asia operations, extending his Asian market experience; joined the group's Leadership Executive in 2011.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Joined Unilever as a marketing trainee
strings.timeline.t8.text: Entered Unilever and subsequently worked in sales and marketing in markets including the UK, Thailand and the United States, building a long international career.
